epistemic_boundary: 2016->2021 is used first as a transparent temporal hindcast and then as a pre-2026 calibration target under the fixed rule below. After calibration it is not described as an untouched holdout; 2026 remains the decisive untouched temporal test.

Bstar_flat_residual_context.role: historical non-hierarchical context only; the frozen hierarchical calibration rule governs F-1 coherence

regional_ballot_bridge.rule: The same sampled national and region innovation affects the 2021 regional-list baseline; the mean local residual sampled within that region supplies the residual bridge.
regional_ballot_bridge.limitation: Only 2021 provides the current regional-list ballot; the bridge is structural and will be scored prospectively in 2026.

minor_party_legal_disaggregation.rule: OTHER is split back into the actual 2021 minor-party codes within each contest in proportion to their 2021 votes before applying the legal allocator.
minor_party_legal_disaggregation.zero_history_rule: A minor party with zero 2021 votes receives zero in F-1; later verified 2026 list entry requires a new B2/F0 snapshot.
minor_party_legal_disaggregation.reason: Treating OTHER as one legal list would manufacture seats and is forbidden.

limitations: Only two modern territorial transitions exist, so the national support is deliberately low-rank and symmetrized rather than presented as a well-estimated full covariance.
The selected scale is calibrated on 2016->2021 under a rule frozen before this execution; it is not an independent validation after selection.
The 2021 regional ballot is bridged structurally because no earlier current-system regional-list ballot exists in the canonical panel.
2026 is the first untouched prospective test of the post-selection calibrated uncertainty layer.
